packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET 07 - UNVERIFIED BLIND IMAGE READING

Exposure statement: Nothing in my context proposed an identification of the work, author, or a prior reading. The only external information visible is the modern pencil shelfmark written on each piece ("Stams, STA, Fag. 164-1r" ... "164-5v") and the directory name; I did not use these to identify anything. I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..026. I also ran `ls` on the packet directory (excluding packet.json from the listing) and `sips` to get the image pixel sizes. Beyond that, I did nothing outside the rules. All 26 images loaded.

====================================================================
1. LAYOUT SURVEY (image-only)
====================================================================
Two overviews: image-001 (recto side of five pieces, pencil labels ending "r"/"n") and image-014 (verso side, labels ending "v"). Tiles: 002-013 cover face 1 (4 columns x 3 rows); 015-026 cover face 2 (same grid). The tiles overlap, so repeated lines are not counted twice.

Pieces (labels as pencilled):
- 164-1 (lower right, largest, about 10 x 13 cm): single column, long lines, German vernacular in a cursive gothic book hand (bastarda-like, single-compartment a, looped ascenders). About 29 lines per face. The left edge has been cut away, so the start of every line is missing (a few letters to about one word). The right edge and the bottom margin survive. Latin quotations are UNDERLINED in brown ink (1r lines 3, 9?, 12; 1v lines 1-4, 20, 27). There are paragraph marks (a tall stroked "¶"/paraph) at 1r "Die erste", 1r "Die dritt", 1v "Dew ander", and 1v "Dew dritt". There is an interlinear addition on 1r above "gelerne". No running title is visible, and no rubrics or coloured initials are visible apart from faint red traces at the edges.
- 164-2 (upper right, horizontal strip): 2r has 4 lines of the same hand, with the left start cut away; 2v is blank (only red specks on the lower edge).
- 164-3 (middle, vertical strip): the right part of a column (3r) or the left part (3v), about 2-4 words per line. On 3v the left margin has marginal marks or notes and paraph-like strokes beside the lines "Du pist ...".
- 164-4 (small piece, lower left): 3 lines on each side.
- 164-5 (narrow vertical strip, left): only the line-initial or line-final letters survive. Tentatively a column edge of the same manuscript. Unreadable as text.

Interpretation (tentative): a vernacular (Bavarian-Austrian forms such as "ai", "ch-", "pist", "dew") homiletic or devotional prose with embedded underlined Latin citations, followed by German renderings ("spricht er ... Ego sum ... Ich pin ..."). 1r expounds three kinds of "warhait" (truth). 1v concerns the Ascension ("gen himel fur", "Er ist heut auff gevaren"). This is an observation of content only, with no identification.

====================================================================
2. SPANS SELECTED
====================================================================
Read: all of 164-1r (lines 1-29) and 164-1v (lines 1-29), all of 2r, 3r/3v as far as the strip allows, and 4r/4v.
Unread or minimal: 164-5r/5v (only isolated letters). The top line of 1v is cut through, so only the descenders are visible. Line starts on 1r/1v are physically lost.

Conventions: [..] marks a physical loss at a cut edge. (x) is a proposed expansion. "?" follows an uncertain reading. Underlining is noted as <u>...</u>. Line numbers are counted from the top of the named tile. Where a line runs across two tiles (008 left half / 009 right half), I give the tile pair, and the number is the line's position in the leaf's text block, which is the same in both tiles.
